input: Test the thesis: GLP-1 drug adoption is a lasting volume headwind for Mondelez

output.thesis: Thesis under test: GLP-1 drug adoption is a lasting volume headwind for Mondelez International's snacking volumes
output.verdict: Partly supported. GLP-1 adoption is a real, growing and measurable drag on US snacking demand — 12% of US adults were on a GLP-1 by late 2025/early 2026, GLP-1 households cut grocery spending 5.3% in six months (savory snacks -10.1%, cookies -7.0%), and cheap pills plus Medicare coverage make the effect more durable. But the evidence that it is a LASTING, Mondelez-specific volume headwind is not yet there: Mondelez attributes its FY2025 volume/mix decline (-3.7%) to cost-of-living pressure, value-seeking and cocoa-led pricing elasticity — never GLP-1 — its volume/mix turned positive (+0.7pp) in Q2 2026 with the FY26 outlook raised to at least 2%, only ~25% of sales are in the US, its core categories (candy/chocolate -3.5%, sweet bakery -8.5%) are hit less than salty snacks, and GLP-1 users are spending MORE on premium chocolate. Verdict: a modest, manageable headwind concentrated in US biscuits/sweet bakery, not yet a proven lasting volume decline; the risk grows materially if oral-pill/Medicare-driven adoption accelerates past current levels.

evidence_for.claim: KFF Health Tracking Poll: 12% of US adults currently taking a GLP-1 for any reason in late 2025, double the 6% measured in May 2024, and the same 12% again in March 2026; Gallup put weight-loss-specific use at 11% in June 2026, up from 3% in 2024 and 8% in 2025 — implying roughly 29-32 million current US users on a ~265m adult population.
Household penetration is broad: Circana put US households with at least one GLP-1 user at 23% of households in November 2025; Numerator 22% in August 2026; PwC 21% in May 2026.

Price and access barriers are falling, making adoption more durable: the Wegovy pill launched January 5, 2026 at $149/month starter dose, Lilly's Foundayo pill followed in April 2026 at the same entry price, Novo Nordisk announced list prices for Wegovy/Ozempic/Rybelsus fall to $675/month from January 2027, and Medicare began covering obesity GLP-1s on July 1, 2026 at a flat $50 copay (GLP-1 Bridge, extended through 2027).

Purchase-receipt data on ~150,000 Numerator households matched to surveys: within six months of adoption, GLP-1 households cut grocery spending 5.3% (higher-income households 8.2%), limited-service restaurant spending fell 8.0%, and savory snacks fell 10.1%.

Category-level detail from the same study: chips and savory snacks down 11.5%, sweet bakery down 8.5%, frozen sides down 7.5%, cheese down 7.2%, cookies down 7.0%, soft drinks down 6.8%, candy and chocolate down 3.5%, alcohol down 1.4% — cookies, sweet bakery and chocolate are all Mondelez categories.

UK: households with a GLP-1 user almost tripled in two years and cut grocery spending by £780m ($1.04bn) in the first year; treat purchases fell — spending on chocolate fell 18 percentage points more than in homes without a user, 75% of users ate less chocolate and 72% ate fewer crisps.

EY-Parthenon survey of 1,700 consumers: GLP-1 adoption 'will be rapid and long-lasting', with usage projected to grow to 13%-21% of US adults (30-50 million people) within 10 years, cutting snacking sales by up to 3% and putting up to a $12 billion dent in snacking market growth ($7bn salty, $5bn sweet snacks).

Morgan Stanley Research: 'Food companies may be among the most exposed' to GLP-1 adoption; discretionary categories — particularly salty snacks and chips — face the greatest pressure, sweet baked goods a similar but slightly more moderate profile; GLP-1 market could reach $190 billion by 2035 with a base case of nearly 30% of the US obese/diabetic population treated by 2035 (up from ~6% in 2025) and 55 million US users by 2035.

J.P. Morgan projects an annual food and beverage revenue reduction of $30-$55 billion by 2030-2034 — 1.2%-2.1% of USDA's $2.58 trillion 2024 US food spending — and 25-30 million Americans on treatment by 2030; Piper Sandler (November 2025) sees a 45-110bp annual headwind on packaged-food sales, cumulating to 325bp by 2028.

Mondelez FY2025 organic net revenue rose 4.3% on 8% pricing and a 3.7% volume/mix decline; category volume/mix fell 7.5% in chocolate, 2.3% in gum & candy and 1.7% in biscuits & baked snacks; North America FY2025 organic revenue fell 1.9% on a 2.7% volume/mix decline — a developed-market volume backdrop consistent with a US demand headwind.

Mondelez CEO Dirk Van de Put noted US biscuit category softness, with 'higher-income consumers increasingly are choosing premium indulgence options alongside better-for-you snacks — particularly those featuring protein' — a demand shift in the same direction GLP-1 research predicts.

Mondelez CEO Dirk Van de Put (CNBC): 'there's a biggest trend towards protein, fiber... that's driven also partly by GLP-1s... those consumers that are on the drug, they want to eat more protein and that is affecting this overall trend' — the company itself acknowledges GLP-1s are reshaping snacking demand.

Circana expects US households with GLP-1 users to account for 35% of all US food and beverage unit sales by 2030; J.P. Morgan forecasts 25 million US GLP-1 users by 2030, a fivefold increase from 2023.

missing_fields: Mondelez-quantified GLP-1 volume/revenue impact (the company discloses none)
Mondelez 10-K risk-factor language on GLP-1 drugs (not found in collected pages)
Q3 2026 (Sep-quarter) Mondelez results and volume/mix — latest reported data available is Q2 2026
Direct peer-comparable estimate of GLP-1 impact specific to Mondelez from sell-side research (only cross-industry estimates: JPM $30-55bn F&B revenue, Piper Sandler 45-110bp packaged-food headwind)
counterarguments: The measured demand effect is smaller than the adoption headlines imply and decays: Circana's own-baseline measurement shows packaged food and beverage spending down only 1.6% after one year, and Numerator's gap narrows to 3.8% after a full year — against 12%+ of adults on the drugs. With only ~25% of Mondelez's sales in the US and ~75% outside it (where GLP-1 use is far less mainstream), the group-level volume exposure is diluted substantially.

Mondelez's core categories are among the LEAST affected: candy/chocolate down only 3.5% versus chips/savory snacks down 11.5% in the household-panel research, and Hartman finds sweeter snacks more resilient than salty. Mondelez is a chocolate and biscuits company (biscuits & baked snacks 48% of FY2025 revenue), not a salty-snacks company.

Churn, not permanence: with 64.8% of non-diabetic users discontinuing within a year and weight regained to baseline in ~1.7 years, the drugged population is a churning stock whose suppressed consumption reverses — so a 'lasting' volume headwind requires persistent net adoption growth, not just current penetration.

Premiumization and mix can offset volume: GLP-1 users spent ~17% more on premium chocolate in 2025 vs 6.5% for non-users, and eMarketer explicitly names Mondelez as a beneficiary — pricing/mix gains (8% FY2025 pricing) have so far more than covered volume declines (organic revenue still +4.3% in FY2025 and +3.0% in Q1 2026).

Mondelez's own trajectory cuts against the thesis: volume/mix swung from -3.7% (FY2025) to a positive +0.7pp contribution in Q2 2026, the FY2026 organic revenue outlook was raised to at least 2%, and management attributes all volume weakness to macro/elasticity factors, never GLP-1.

The company is actively hedging the trend: better-for-you crackers and protein bars, gluten-free and zero-added-sugar Oreo, Builder's/Perfect Snacks protein brands (which the CEO says carry protein 'rather than adding protein to core brands like Oreos'), and portion-controlled price-pack architecture — adaptation that blunts the volume impact.

evidence_against.claim: Mondelez Q2 2026 organic sales rose 2.2% with volume and mix CONTRIBUTING +0.7 percentage points (pricing +1.5pp) — volumes inflected positive; the company raised its FY2026 organic revenue outlook to at least 2% and increased its quarterly dividend 4%, citing robust top-line expansion, volume growth and share improvement.

Mondelez attributes its FY2025 volume/mix decline (-3.7%) to consumer cost-of-living pressures, value-seeking, cocoa-led pricing elasticity and price-pack architecture changes — management never attributes any volume decline to GLP-1 drugs, and the article contains no mention of GLP-1.

Mondelez CEO Dirk Van de Put: 'I think the whole topic has been overblown... It's really not a big concern for us at this stage'; 'We're talking about 0.5% to 1% volume effect ten years down the road.' He also noted ~75% of sales are outside the US and ~20% of sales are snacks under 200 calories, with BelVita and snack bars fitting 'perfectly into the diet of GLP-1 patients.'

Persistence is poor: in a cohort of 125,000 US adults with overweight/obesity and no diabetes, 64.8% had discontinued GLP-1s within a year and 84.4% within two years; a BMJ meta-analysis of 37 studies found patients regain about 4.8 kg in the year after stopping and return to baseline weight in roughly 1.7 years — the on-drug population is a churning stock, so the consumption effect is temporary per household.

The measured spending gap shrinks over time: Numerator's August 2026 tracker found the grocery gap narrowing to 3.8% after a full year (items per trip down just 3.7%), and Circana — measuring users against their own pre-adoption baseline — found packaged food and beverage spending down only 1.6% after one year, with total restaurant spending UP 0.9%.

Chocolate is a counter-signal: per Lindt & Sprüngli citing Circana, 15% of US households had GLP-1 members as of February yet accounted for 17.5% of chocolate sales; US GLP-1 users spent almost 17% more on premium chocolate in 2025 vs a 6.5% increase among non-users — eMarketer calls this 'good news for Lindt, Mondelez, and other companies whose business relies on the sale of indulgent treats.'

Hartman Group research (1,000+ US GLP-1 users): sweeter snacks are proving more 'resilient' than salty snacks, partly due to nostalgia; GlobalData notes 'smaller quantities do not necessarily mean consumers disengage from these categories altogether' — indulgence becomes more intentional (smaller portions, fewer occasions) rather than a category exit.

Mondelez emerging markets (India, Brazil, China) grew ahead of expectations with double-digit increases in chocolate and biscuits; developed markets stabilized with improving share trends in European chocolate and North American crackers; the Q1 2026 earnings-call coverage contains no mention of GLP-1 drugs at all.

Mondelez official Q1 2026 release: net revenues +8.2%, Organic Net Revenue growth +3.0% driven by higher net pricing, partially offset by unfavorable volume/mix — no GLP-1 reference anywhere in the release's first-quarter commentary.

CEO Van de Put (CNBC, Nov 2026): snacking overall is 'resilient' with 'a little bit of volume growth' today; strong emerging-market growth (India, Brazil); consumers on GLP-1s are 'not completely abandoning' indulgent snacks — 'there's still good growth there'; growth has inflected to volume growth as pricing comes down.

Mondelez is adapting its portfolio to the health/protein shift — accelerating innovation in better-for-you crackers and protein bars (plus gluten-free and zero-added-sugar Oreo, protein/fiber launches per the Q1 2026 call) — and adapting price-pack architecture, which can offset a portion of any GLP-1-driven demand change.

key_uncertainties: Whether any portion of Mondelez's FY2025 volume/mix decline (-3.7%, chocolate -7.5%) is GLP-1-attributable: management attributes it entirely to cost-of-living pressure, value-seeking and cocoa-led pricing elasticity, and the company has never quantified a GLP-1 impact — so the thesis cannot be confirmed or refuted from company disclosure.

Whether Mondelez's 10-K risk factors now list GLP-1 drugs (peers such as RBI and Dutch Bros added GLP-1 to their 10-K risk factors in fiscal 2025); this was not verifiable in the collected pages and would signal how the company itself frames the risk.

How quickly the 2026-2027 access accelerants (Wegovy pill at $149/month, Foundayo, list prices falling to $675/month from January 2027, Medicare $50 copay coverage through 2027) push adoption beyond the current ~12% of US adults — Morgan Stanley already raised its 2035 US-user projection to 55 million in April 2026, but the elasticity of adoption to price is unknown.

Whether international GLP-1 penetration converges toward US levels: UK GLP-1 households nearly tripled in two years and cut chocolate spending 18pp more than non-user homes (Worldpanel), but industry voices note GLP-1 use is 'way less mainstream in Europe' — Mondelez's largest region is Europe, so its trajectory there is pivotal.

Whether habits persist after discontinuation: EY-Parthenon notes it is 'unclear what would happen to people's habits after they stop using the drugs, or whether there would be a lasting impact on users' health and consumption patterns' — this single unknown largely determines whether the headwind is lasting or cyclical.
Q3 2026 results (quarter ended September 30, 2026) were not available in the collected pages; they would show whether the Q2 2026 volume/mix inflection (+0.7pp) held or reverted.
what_would_change_the_view: Mondelez quantifying a GLP-1 impact on an earnings call, or adding GLP-1/weight-loss drugs to its 10-K risk factors (as RBI and Dutch Bros did in fiscal 2025) — a management admission would materially strengthen the thesis.

US biscuit/baked-snack and chocolate volume/mix turning materially negative for two or more consecutive quarters (vs the Q2 2026 +0.7pp positive), especially while management stops attributing weakness to pricing elasticity and cost-of-living.

Adoption accelerating clearly past ~12% of US adults — e.g., survey or IQVIA data showing 15%+ of adults on GLP-1s by end-2027 as $149/month pills and Medicare coverage scale, or Circana's forecast of GLP-1 households reaching 35% of US food & beverage unit sales by 2030 tracking ahead of schedule.

Peer chocolate/biscuit makers (Hershey, Lindt, Nestlé, Ferrero) attributing volume declines to GLP-1 in their disclosures — the current peer evidence points the other way (Lindt reports chocolate sales growing faster among GLP-1 households).

European or emerging-market adoption data (Worldpanel/IGD, or China/Brazil patent expiries and generics cutting prices up to 70%) showing Mondelez's non-US geographies beginning to replicate the US category declines — this would break the '75% of sales outside the US' defense.

Conversely, the view weakens if volume/mix stays positive through 2026-2027 while the company sustains ≥2% organic growth — indicating pricing/mix, premiumization and portfolio adaptation fully absorb the GLP-1 drag.
